note_text: Patient is a 64-year-old with pernicious anemia followed for several years, previously documented with low serum B12 (last checked prior to therapy: 148 pg/mL, MCV elevated at 104). She has a history of glossitis and mild peripheral paresthesias attributable to B12 deficiency. She is currently undergoing chemotherapy for malignant pleural mesothelioma with pemetrexed/cisplatin. She tolerated her most recent infusion cycle without significant nausea; mild fatigue reported. Folic acid supplementation continues at 1 mg daily as part of her regimen. Neurologic exam today shows stable decreased vibratory sensation in the toes bilaterally, unchanged from baseline. Labs today notable for stable hemoglobin and unremarkable renal function. Plan: continue pemetrexed per oncology schedule, continue folic acid, follow up B12 level at next visit, monitor for peripheral neuropathy progression.
